question: A man has invested ₹65,000 at a rate of 7(1)/(2)\% per annum simple interest for 6 years. Find the amount that he will receive after 6 years.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Total Interest Percentage = Rate × Time

Total % = 7.5% × 6 = 45%

Amount = Principal + 45% of Principal = 145% of ₹65,000

Amount = 1.45 × 65000 = ₹94,250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹94,250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = **₹65,000**

Rate (R) = 7.5% = **15/2%**

Time (T) = **6 years**

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = Principal + Simple Interest
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9929d125b85ed68b8381715f27d758df86da8004e49d6dd16d99e676b421a5cb.png] 
**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (65000 × 15 × 6) ÷ (2 × 100)

⇒ SI = 650 × 15 × 3

⇒ SI = 650 × 45

⇒ SI = **₹29,250**

⇒ Amount = 65000 + 29250

⇒ Amount = **₹94,250**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹94,250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest is calculated only on the principal, whereas in Compound Interest, it is calculated on the principal plus accumulated interest.

Effective Rate of Interest

Effective Rate for T years = (Rate × T)%. The final amount is always (100 + RT)% of the Principal.
